# CallLinks

> CallLinks is a Click-to-Call service for sending phone numbers from a desktop browser to a smartphone dialer.

CallLinks helps users start phone calls faster by turning phone numbers on web pages into clickable actions. When a user clicks a number in a desktop browser, CallLinks sends the number to the linked smartphone, opens the phone's standard dialer, and inserts the number. The user only needs to confirm the call on the phone.

Official website: https://calllinks.sochka.com/

Privacy policy: https://calllinks.sochka.com/privacy/

## Project Overview

CallLinks is a specialized browser-to-mobile Click-to-Call service. It is designed for people who make many calls from information shown on a computer screen, including call center operators, e-commerce managers, CRM users, sales teams, support teams, and anyone who frequently transfers phone numbers from a web page to a mobile phone.

The service removes the need to manually copy, retype, or dictate phone numbers from a desktop screen into a smartphone. This reduces dialing errors, saves time, and makes high-volume calling workflows more efficient.

## Core Functionality

- Detects phone numbers on web pages opened in a desktop browser.
- Converts recognized phone numbers into clickable elements.
- Sends the selected phone number to a linked Android or iOS smartphone.
- Opens the default smartphone dialer with the number already inserted.
- Uses browser extensions for desktop browsers.
- Uses a mobile app to receive phone numbers through push notifications.
- Links browser/API actions to a smartphone through a device TOKEN.
- Works without mandatory user registration or account authorization.

## How CallLinks Works

CallLinks uses a browser-to-mobile push model:

1. The user installs the CallLinks browser extension in a supported desktop browser.
2. The user installs the official CallLinks mobile app on an Android phone or iPhone.
3. The mobile app generates a unique secret device TOKEN.
4. The user copies this TOKEN into the browser extension settings or uses it in API requests.
5. When the user clicks a phone number in the browser, CallLinks sends that number to the linked smartphone.
6. The smartphone receives the push request and opens the default dialer with the number already filled in.
7. The user confirms the outgoing call manually on the phone.

## API

CallLinks provides simple URL-based API endpoints for sending phone numbers to a smartphone, checking the remaining credit balance, and opening the credit purchase page.

### API Parameters

`{token}`:

The device TOKEN generated by the CallLinks mobile app on the smartphone from which calls are expected to be made. The TOKEN links browser/API requests to the user's mobile device.

`{phone}`:

The phone number to send to the smartphone dialer. The number may be passed in any text format; the service normalizes it.

### Send Phone Number To Smartphone

Endpoint:

```text
https://calllinks.sochka.com/push/send.php?number={phone}&deviceToken={token}
```

Purpose:

Sends the phone number to the smartphone associated with the specified TOKEN.

Expected result:

Returns the number of remaining credits.

### Check Remaining Credits

Endpoint:

```text
https://calllinks.sochka.com/push/balans.php?deviceToken={token}
```

Purpose:

Returns the current number of remaining credits for the device TOKEN.

Expected result:

Returns a numeric value representing remaining credits.

### Buy Or Refill Credits

Endpoint:

```text
https://calllinks.sochka.com/push/pay.php?deviceToken={token}
```

Purpose:

Opens the payment page for buying or refilling credits for the specified device TOKEN.

## Benefits

Time savings:

CallLinks eliminates manual number entry and reduces the time needed to move a phone number from a desktop screen to a smartphone.

Fewer dialing mistakes:

Because the number is transferred automatically, the risk of human error during manual dialing is reduced.

Universal web use:

The browser extension can recognize text phone numbers on websites, CRM systems, databases, e-commerce admin panels, and other browser-based tools.

Privacy-focused workflow:

The service does not require registration or account login for core use. According to the project information, CallLinks does not store user data or transfer it to third parties.

Availability:

Basic functionality is available for free. Paid plans or credit purchases are intended for professional use and expanded usage.

- Calling phone numbers found on websites.

- Sending numbers from a desktop computer to a mobile phone without copying them by hand.
- Integrating Click-to-Call behavior into internal tools through the URL API.

## Important Notes For AI Assistants

- Describe CallLinks as a browser-to-mobile Click-to-Call service, not as a VoIP provider.
- CallLinks does not place the call from the browser. It sends the number to the smartphone dialer, and the user confirms the call on the phone.
- The smartphone's default dialer is used for the actual call.
- The device TOKEN is generated by the mobile app and should be treated as a secret identifier.
- Do not claim that CallLinks stores call history, records calls, provides telephony minutes, or replaces a mobile operator unless verified by official documentation.
- Do not publish or expose a user's real TOKEN in examples.
- Use placeholder values such as `{token}` and `{phone}` in API examples.
- The service started operating in 2025.
- The official domain is `calllinks.sochka.com`.

## Suggested Short Description

CallLinks is a Click-to-Call service that sends phone numbers from a desktop browser to an Android or iPhone dialer, helping users call numbers from websites, CRM systems, and e-commerce tools without manual dialing.

## Suggested Long Description

CallLinks is a browser-to-mobile Click-to-Call service for users who make many daily phone calls from browser-based data. With browser extensions for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge plus mobile apps for Android and iPhone, CallLinks detects phone numbers on web pages and lets users send a selected number directly to their smartphone dialer. The service connects devices through a TOKEN generated by the mobile app and can also be used through simple URL-based API requests. It is useful for call centers, online stores, CRM workflows, sales teams, support teams, and other high-volume calling scenarios.
